summary: Fragmented slot saturation from many small streaming sessions causing sustained throughput degradation
description:
Issue summary: Customer reported sustained drop in throughput and elevated latency on their Dedicated pool while overall GPU utilization remained moderate. Impact: Several endpoints serving short streaming requests experienced p95/p99 latency increases and request queuing; customers observed degraded conversational responsiveness. Environment: prod, dedicated pool (us-west, eu-central).

Observed behavior: Autoscaler did not add capacity despite aggregated utilization appearing below threshold (~65%). Investigation showed large number of concurrent short-lived streaming sessions (average 120ms open time) causing slot fragmentation: GPUs had many partially-filled slots that prevented efficient batching. Scheduler metrics indicate high slot fragmentation ratio and 'fractional_slot' counts per GPU.

Expected behavior: Small streaming workloads should coalesce onto fewer GPUs and autoscaler should trigger when effective available full-slot capacity falls below target.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Spawn 2k concurrent streaming connections that send brief (1-3 token) heartbeats every second. 2) Target a dedicated pool configured with slot size 8 and autoscale thresholds at 75% aggregate utilization. 3) Observe scheduler slot allocation, GPU fractional_slot counts, and autoscaler decision loop.

Relevant logs/metrics: scheduler.alloc_log (timestamps and slot assignments), autoscaler.eval.trace (no scale-up events observed for 30m), serving_runtime.kernel-warn entries showing fragmented batch sizes, console dashboards showing p95 latency jumps.

Customer impact: Medium-to-high for affected routes; several customer-facing flows experienced several-second tail latency spikes during peak small-stream bursts.
comments: 2026-02-18 Priya Desai: Customer (Acme AI) reported p95 latency on chat routes increased from 240ms to ~1800ms during morning burst; attached request traces and sample logs. Notified SRE team and opened ticket.

2026-02-18 Elena Kim (SRE): Initial triage indicates many short-lived streaming sessions. GPU utilization metric looks normal but scheduler shows high fractional_slot counts. Hypothesis: fragmentation prevents batch formation, reducing effective throughput.

2026-02-19 Rajesh Patel (Acme AI): We saw this most strongly after a product change that split long conversations into micro-chunks for perceived interactivity. Can we throttle or coalesce on the platform side until we change client behavior?

2026-02-20 Marco Alvarez (Eng): Rolled a quick patch to scheduler that biases coalescing of small streams into shared slots and added a heuristic to the autoscaler to consider 'effective_available_slots' instead of raw GPU utilization. Deployed to staging for smoke tests.

2026-02-22 Marco Alvarez: Staging tests show p95 latency improvement from 1.6s -> 300ms under the synthetic small-stream workload. PR merged and progressively rolled to prod for two dedicated pools starting 2026-02-23.

2026-02-25 Priya Desai: Customer confirmed improved latency; closing incident. Customer followed suggested short-term workaround of enabling client-side request coalescing in their SDK while platform changes rolled out.
investigation_notes: Collected scheduler allocation logs and traced slot assignment hot paths; identified GPUs with >40 fractional slots consistently during bursts.

Replayed workload in staging with synthetic short streaming clients to reproduce fragmentation; observed autoscaler threshold logic ignored fragmentation because aggregate utilization stayed below 75%.
Profiled serving runtime: kernel invocation rates were high with small batch sizes leading to increased per-request overhead and jitter in latency.

Tested autoscaler change: compute 'effective_available_slots' = sum(floor(available_capacity/slot_size)) across GPUs; scale-up triggered correctly on test runs when effective slots fell below low-water mark.

Evaluated alternate mitigations: (a) increase slot packing aggressiveness, (b) add per-tenant aggregation proxy, (c) customer SDK coalescing. Opted to implement (a) + autoscaler heuristic and recommend (c) as a short-term customer-side mitigation.
No evidence of tenant eviction or GPU hardware errors; this is scheduling and placement inefficiency under many small streaming connections.
resolution_summary: Deployed scheduler patch to improve coalescing of short-lived streaming sessions and updated autoscaler heuristic to account for slot fragmentation (effective_available_slots). Customer also enabled client-side coalescing as a short-term workaround. Post-deployment metrics show p95 latency reduced from ~1.6s to ~300ms and request queuing eliminated for affected routes.
follow_up_actions: Create a new monitoring metric 'slot_fragmentation_ratio' and add alert when ratio > 0.35 in dedicated pools.
Update autoscaler runbook to include fragmentation-aware checks and remediation steps.
Add a lightweight SDK feature guide for recommended client-side coalescing for streaming workloads.
Include fragmentation simulation in our soak tests to catch regressions in future releases.
